title: Pentagon budget bill would loosen restrictions on military flights near Reagan National Airport
summary: A Pentagon spending bill that passed the House and is heading to the Senate includes language that weakens some of the reforms on military flights near Reagan National Airport after a Jan. 29 crash that killed 67 people.
content:
By Dan Ronan

A Pentagon budget bill that passed the House and is heading to the Senate includes language that weakens some of the reforms on military flights near Reagan National Airport that were imposed after a Jan. 29 crash that killed 67 people.

An Army Black Hawk helicopter collided with an American Airlines regional jet that was coming in for a landing at National that night, killing all 67 people in both aircraft.

The language in the $900 billion bill, which caught many people off guard, was described by National Transportation Safety Board Chair Jennifer Homendy as “shameful.”

“It represents an unacceptable risk to the flying public, to commercial and military aircraft, crews and to the residents in the region,” Homendy said Wednesday. “It’s also an unthinkable dismissal of our investigation and of 67 families … who lost loved ones in a tragedy that was entirely preventable.”

The NTSB has no regulatory authority and can only make recommendations about ways to improve transportation safety, and Homendy’s strong remarks about the legislation caught many by surprise.

Aviation safety analyst Jeff Guzzetti, who worked for the NTSB and the Federal Aviation Administration before becoming an analyst at NBC News, said Homendy has put a stake in the ground when it comes to safety around Reagan National.

“This House language greatly weakens safety to the point where she believes the airspace around DCA [National] will be unsafe,” Guzzetti said. “Her interpretation of this legislation is that it rolls back things before the mid-air collision/accident, and she finds that unacceptable.”

Specifically, Homendy and several senators pointed to language in the House bill that includes exceptions to let military helicopters fly through the crowded airspace around the nation’s capital without using technology called Automatic Dependent Surveillance Broadcast, or ADS-B, to broadcast aircraft location data to other planes and air traffic controllers.

ADS-B transmissions allow pilots in nearby airspace to track in real-time the exact locations of other commercial planes, helicopters and general aviation planes, providing an extra level of safety so aviators can avoid collisions. A little more than a month after the crash, the FAA began requiring military pilots to use ADS-B when flying.

The transmissions are not encrypted, however, and the information is available on numerous websites. Many in the military do not want the flights tracked, especially if they are carrying high-ranking government officials.

Homendy said when it comes to determining safety risks, the military aren’t the experts. In the years before the crash, there were 85 close calls near National between military helicopters and commercial jets, and neither the Pentagon nor the Army noticed the deteriorating safety situation. Homendy also said that no one on Capitol Hill bothered to consult with the NTSB on the bill.

“Chair Homendy wasn’t getting satisfaction from the many phone calls she was attempting to make to the House committees,” Guzzetti said. He said that restrictions after the crash that strictly limit military helicopter flights near National are working, because history has shown that allowing low-flying helicopters at night near a crowded airport, as was the case in January, is too dangerous.

“She is using the bully pulpit of the NTSB to get her message across,” he said of Homendy.

Officials react

Sen. Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), the chairman of the Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation, Space, and Innovation, said Thursday the National Defense Authorization Act fails to implement minimum standards for military helicopters operating in mixed airspace, such as Reagan National. Moran wants the legislation amended: Several of the people on the American Airlines fights were from his state and the plane had taken off from Wichita.

Sens. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) and Ted Cruz (R-Texas) filed amendments to the legislation to remove the helicopter safety provisions, saying in a joint statement, “We owe it to the families to put into law actual safety improvements, not give the Department of Defense bigger loopholes to exploit.”

Both of Virginia’s senators also criticized the proposed changes.

“The language in this provision could allow rolling back crucial new safety practices I fought to implement after the Jan. 29 tragedy, and give the Department of Defense more discretion over safety procedures in the region,” Sen. Mark Warner (D-Va.) said in a statement.

He said the Pentagon needs more supervision and regulation, not less.

“It’s clear that we cannot rely on the DoD alone to be the safety authority over its flights in this area,” Warner’s statement stressed.

Sen. Tim Kaine (D-Va.) has been one of the leaders to tighten airspace and other flight restrictions at National.

Future movements

The NTSB’s final report on the cause of the collision is expected mid-2026. Investigators have already determined the Black Hawk was flying too low on a helicopter route that provided minimal separation between jets and helicopters approaching Reagan’s secondary Runway 33, which the regional jet was about to land on.

An estimated 20 seconds before the crash, the jet’s two pilots did get a warning. However, because the jet was at such a low altitude, just over 310 feet, the collision avoidance system is only partially enabled to prevent false alarms because there is little room to maneuver.

President Donald Trump said he wants to sign the bill because it advances many of his priorities and it also provides a 3.8% pay hike for many in the military.

The Senate could take up the legislation next week, and it appears unlikely that any final changes will be made. But Congress is leaving for a holiday break at the end of the week, and the defense bill is considered something that must pass by the end of the year.
author: WTOP News
